False: models/2014-raspopovic-bmp-sox9-wnt-digits.py (2,066 lines, Pass 3: Bmp-Sox9-Wnt 3-node RD on a growing polar-fan limb-bud mesh, Crampin-Gaffney-Maini dilution) and models/2012-sheth-hox-turing-polydactyly.py (1,619 lines) already exist. Caught by the Claude Fable panellist, verified by the aggregator. The provisional tool_fit (9/25) under-priced this problem; the panel scores stand as recorded, and a re-score with the corrected route is the next action on TOP-06.

gemini-4-argon.label: Gemini 4 Argon Medium
gemini-4-argon.note: The crux is that achieving >=95% topological locking of exactly 5 rays from unseeded random initial conditions on a finite-difference fan grid is notoriously sensitive to boundary no-flux discretization and growth rate schedules. Even if the script finishes, the hypothesis as stated (>=95% five-ray success) will very likely be refuted unless pre-existing AP polarity (Shh/Gli3 gradient) is also included.

gemini-4-argon.label: Gemini 4 Argon Medium
gemini-4-argon.note: The crux is fundamental symmetry: Meinhardt-Klingler's 1D diffusion operator d^2/dx^2 is reflection-symmetric (left-right invariant), whereas Rule 30 breaks left-right symmetry via a_{i-1} XOR (a_i OR a_{i+1}). Thus the transducer test will reach a fast, decisive verdict—almost certainly proving that isotropic Meinhardt PDE reduces to a symmetric elementary CA class (like Rule 90/18) rather than chiral Rule 30 unless oblique wave travel or asymmetric coupling is present.

gemini-4-argon.label: Gemini 4 Argon Medium
gemini-4-argon.note: The crux—explicitly proved by Tarnita et al. (2017)—is that macro-scale fairy-circle centroids from both termite territory competition and scale-dependent water-vegetation feedback converge to the same hexagonal packing limit (6 neighbors, identical g(r) first peak). Only multi-scale sub-meter vegetation patterning between circles or temporal birth-death trajectories can separate the two mechanisms.
